# DatePart

Gives one part of a date, such as its year or its day of the week, as a number.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
DatePart(date, part)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | string | The date to read: a string in one of the forms `ParseDate` accepts. A string in no accepted form is a runtime error, as is any other type, null included. |
| `part` | string | The part to give, one of `"year"`, `"month"` (1 to 12), `"day"` (the day of the month, from 1), `"hour"` (0 to 23), `"minute"`, `"second"`, `"dayofweek"` (0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday) or `"dayofyear"` (1 to 366), matched with no regard to the case of ASCII letters. Any other string is a runtime error, as is a value that is not a string, null included. |

## Returns

Number. The part asked for, as a whole number. Never null.

## Remarks

The part is taken from the date in UTC.

## Example

`DatePart("2024-01-15T09:30:00Z", "hour")` returns 9.

`DatePart("2024-01-15", "dayofweek")` returns 1.
